lessons.title: How to identify a plant
lessons.html:
Why identification matters

A horticulture worker must know the plants on site. You need to know a plant's name to water, feed and prune it correctly, to pick the right plant for an order, and to tell a weed from a valuable plant. You also need to know which plants are poisonous or invasive.

Common and botanical names

Most plants have a common name and a botanical (scientific) name. Common names change from place to place. "Wild dagga", for example, is a common name. The botanical name, Leonotis leonurus, is the same all over the world. A botanical name has two parts:

  • Genus – the first word, with a capital letter, e.g. Agapanthus.
  • Species – the second word, small letter, e.g. praecox.

A cultivar name in quotes may follow, e.g. Agapanthus 'Snowball'. Nursery labels use botanical names, so learn them.

What to look at

  • Growth form – tree, shrub, climber, groundcover, grass, bulb, succulent.
  • Leaves – shape, size, edge (smooth, toothed), arrangement (opposite or alternate), colour, smell when crushed.
  • Flowers – colour, shape, season.
  • Stems and bark – thorns, colour, texture.
  • Fruit and seeds.

Use a plant book, the nursery labels, and ask your supervisor. Practise by walking the site and naming each plant every day.

lessons.title: Common ornamental plants in South Africa
lessons.html:
Indigenous plants

South Africa has one of the richest floras in the world. Many indigenous plants are used in gardens because they cope with local conditions and use less water.

Common nameBotanical nameType and notes
AgapanthusAgapanthus praecoxClump-forming perennial, blue or white summer flowers
Bird of paradiseStrelitzia reginaeOrange and blue flowers like a bird's head
Wild daggaLeonotis leonurusShrub, orange tubular flowers, attracts sunbirds
PlumbagoPlumbago auriculataScrambling shrub, pale blue flowers, good hedge
SpekboomPortulacaria afraSucculent shrub, very drought tolerant
King proteaProtea cynaroidesShrub with very large flower heads; national flower
Wild irisDietes grandifloraTough clump plant with white flowers
Cape honeysuckleTecoma capensisScrambling shrub, orange flowers

Exotic ornamentals

  • Roses (Rosa) – shrubs with thorny stems.
  • Azaleas (Rhododendron) – shade shrubs with spring flowers, like acid soil.
  • Hydrangeas – large leaves and flower heads; flower colour changes with soil acidity.
  • Lavender (Lavandula) – grey, scented leaves.

Plants to be careful with

  • Invasive aliens – some plants spread into the veld and use water, for example lantana (Lantana camara) and syringa (Melia azedarach). They are regulated and must not be planted. Report them.
  • Poisonous plants – oleander (Nerium oleander) is poisonous to people and animals. Euphorbia sap can burn skin and eyes. Wear gloves and wash hands.

Key points

  • Botanical names (genus and species) are the same everywhere; learn them.
  • Identify plants by growth form, leaves, flowers, stems and fruit.
  • Know common indigenous plants such as agapanthus, strelitzia, plumbago and spekboom.
  • Recognise and report invasive plants such as lantana.
  • Know poisonous plants like oleander and handle them with gloves.
